title: Proof
body_md:
Since by (\ref{decomp3}) $\log|h'|$ is a positive harmonic function in $H$ it can be represented (cf. \cite[p. 149]{T})
$$
\log| h'(\zeta)|=\frac {\sigma} \pi\int_{-\infty}^\infty\frac{\log|h'(is)|ds}{|\zeta -is|^2}+c\,\zeta\qquad c\geq 0  .
$$
Furthermore, by \cite[Theorem IV. 19.]{T}, $\log h'(\zeta)/\zeta\to c$ and 
$h''(\zeta)/h'(\zeta)\to c$ in $S_\epsilon$.  By \cite[Lemma 2]{W1} it follows that $c=0$.

\qed

title: Lemma
head: manual

title: Proof
body_md:
For notational simplicity we shall replace $z/r_m,\  r_m'/r_m,\ r_m''/r_m,\ u(r_mz)/r_m,$ and $ M_n$ by $z,\ r,\ R,\ u(z),$ and $ M$
respectively.

Following Mikljukov, we choose the density function
$$
\rho(z)=(|z|^2+u^2(z))^{-1/2},
$$
for $z\in B=\overline T\cap \overline{D(r,R)}$ and $\rho(z)=0$ for all the remaining
values $\ z\in D$.  Hence
\begin{equation}
\label{4.3}
\text{\rm mod}_F \Gamma \le {\displaystyle\iint_B (|z|^2+u^2(z))^{-1}d\sigma_F\over
\left(\underset{\gamma\in\Gamma}{\inf} \int_\gamma (|z|^2+u^2(z))^{-1/2}ds_F\right)^2}.
\end{equation}

For the denominator in (\ref{4.3}), let $\gamma$ be a curve in $\Gamma$.   Then
\begin{equation}
\label{4.4}
\int_\gamma \rho\, ds_F = \int_\gamma (|z|^2+u^2(z))^{-1/2} ds_F\ge \log\left(1+{R-r\over M}\right).
\end{equation}


To obtain a bound for the numerator we let
\begin{equation}
\label{4.5a}
\eta(z)={1\over |z|}\,\arctan \delta(z),\qquad \delta(z)={u(z)\over |z|},
\end{equation}
so that
\begin{equation}
\label{4.5b}
{1\over |z|^2+u^2(z)}={1\over |z|^2(1+\delta^2(z))}.
\end{equation}

To begin with, we note that
$$
\eta_{x_i}={-x_i\over |z|^3}\,\arctan \delta(z)+{1\over|z|} {1\over 1+\delta^2(z)}\left({u_{x_i}\over |z|}-{x_iu\over |z|^3}\right),
$$
and so
\begin{equation}
\label{4.6}
\sum_{i=1}^2 {u^2_{x_i}\over |z|^2(1+\delta^2(z))\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}\\ =
 \sum_{i=1}^2 {\eta_{x_i}u_{x_i}\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}
 \end{equation}
 $$
+{\arctan \delta(z)\over |z|^3} \sum_{i=1}^2 {x_iu_{x_i}\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}
+{1\over |z|^3} {\delta(z)\over 1+\delta^2(z)} \sum_{i=1}^2
{x_iu_{x_i}\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}.
$$
Also,
$$
\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}={1\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}+\sum_{i=1}^2
{u_{x_i}^2\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}},
$$
and thus 
\begin{equation}
\label{4.7}
\sum_{i=1}^2 {u^2_{x_i}\over |z|^2(1+\delta^2(z))\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}} =
{\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}\over |z|^2(1+\delta^2(z))}
\end{equation}
$$
-{1\over 
|z|^2(1+\delta^2(z))\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}.
$$

Finally, by Green's Theorem
\begin{equation}
\label{4.8}
\iint_B \sum_{i=1}^2 {\eta_{x_i}u_{x_i}\over\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}\,dx_1dx_2+
\iint_B \eta \sum_{i=1}^2 {\partial\over\partial x_i} {u_{x_i}\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}\,dx_1dx_2
\end{equation}
$$
= \int_{\partial B} {\eta \nabla u\cdot n\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}} |dz|,
$$
with $n$ being the outer unit normal.   
The middle term vanishes because of the minimal surface equation.    

Using (4.5)--(4.7) in (4.8) we then have
   
                                                           
                                        
   

$$
\iint_B {d\sigma_F\over|z|^2+u^2(z)} = 
\iint_B {1\over (1+\delta^2(z))\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}
{dx_1dx_2\over |z|^2}
$$
$$
+ \int_{\partial B} {\eta \nabla u\cdot n\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}\,|dz|
+\iint_B  \arctan \delta(z)\  \sum_{i=1}^2 
{x_iu_{x_i}\over |z|\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}{dx_1dx_2\over |z|^2}
$$
$$
+ \iint_B {\delta(z)\over 1+\delta^2(z)}\ \sum_{i=1}^2 
{x_iu_{x_i}\over
|z|\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}} {dx_1dx_2\over |z|^2}\\
$$
Since 
$$
\sum_{i=1}^2 {x_iu_{x_i}\over |z|\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}\le
{|\nabla u|\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}},
$$
this gives
$$
\iint_B {d\sigma_F\over|z|^2+u^2(z)} \le 
   \iint_B 
{1\over (1+\delta^2(z))\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}{dx_1dx_2\over |z|^2}
$$
$$
+\int_{\partial B} {\eta\nabla u\cdot n\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}
{|dz|\over |z|}
+ \iint_B \arctan \delta(z){|\nabla u|\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}
{dx_1dx_2\over |z|^2}
$$
$$
+\iint_B {\delta(z)\over 1+\delta^2(z)}
{|\nabla u|\over \sqrt{1+ |\nabla u|^2}}{dx_1dx_2\over |z|^2}.
$$ 
Since
$$
\displaystyle\int_{\partial B} {\eta\nabla u\cdot n\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}{|dz|\over |z|}\le 
\displaystyle\int_{\partial B} {\eta |\nabla u|\over \sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}{|dz|\over |z|}\le 2\pi^2,
$$
we have
$$
\iint_B {d\sigma_F\over |z|^2+u^2(z)}\le \iint_B \frac1{\sqrt{1+\nabla u|^2}}
 (\frac 1{1+\delta^2(z)}
$$
$$
+|\nabla u|\arctan\delta (z)+
\frac{|\nabla u|\delta (z)}{1+\delta^2(z)})
(1+o(1)) {dx_1dx_2\over |z|^2}
+2\pi^2 \quad (R\to \infty).
$$
By letting $\delta (z)\to \infty$ and using (\ref{initial1}) we obtain
  (\ref {4.2a}).  Using (\ref{initial 1a}) and lettting $\delta\to 0$ we obtain
  (\ref{4.2aa}).
  
   \qed

head: manual

title: Lemma
body_md:
\emph{Let $D$ be an unbounded simply connected 
domain with with $\Theta(r_n)\leq\beta<\pi$
    for an increasing sequence $r_n\to\infty$.
    If $u$ is a solution to the boundary value problem (\ref{mineq1}). 
then there exists a sequence $r_n'<r_n$ such that $r_{n}/r_n'\leq B$ for some $B>0$. 
and a constant $K=K(\beta,B )$, such that }
$$
u(z)\leq Kr_n\qquad z\in D\cap\{|z|=r_n'\}.
$$
head: manual

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\gamma$ be an arc on the unit disk having length 
$\beta$ 
and $\ell$ be the line segment joining the endpoints of $\beta$. Let $V$ be the subset of the disk having its boundary as $\ell$ and the complement of $\beta$ with respect
to the boundary of the disk.

Extend $\ell$ symmetrically to length 1, and let $\tilde\ell$ be the line formed by translating
the extended $\ell$ parallel to itself 10 units in the direction of the origin. Now construct
a rectangle $R$ by joining the endpoints of the extended $\ell$ to the endpoints of 
$\tilde\ell$.  Then $V\subset R$ and it follows from \cite[p. 322]{JS}
that there exists a solution $v(z)$ to the minimal surface equation in $R$ having boundary values $+\infty$ on the extended $\ell$ and $\tilde\ell$, and 0 on the other two sides.



 Let $\eta$ be the distance from the origin to $\ell$
and $\Delta=\{|z|<\eta/2\}$.  Let $M$ denote the maximum of $v(z)$ in $\Delta$.

Now, for any given $r_n$, the function $u(r_nz)/r_n$ satisfies the minimal surface equation
and we consider any of the components of the set where $u(r_nz)>0$ in
 $|z|<1$.  In any such component $u(r_nz)/r_n$
is bounded by the corresponding $v(z)$ with the arc $\gamma$ referred to above, being
an arc containing the portion of the component on the boundary.  Thus, if the component
extends to $\Delta$, then for those points in $\Delta$ we have
$u(r_nz)/r_n\leq M$.  Applying this to all such components we then get $u(z)
\leq Mr_n$ for $z\in D\cap\{|z|=\eta\, r_n/2\}$ from which the result follows.

\qed

label: Poisson2
title: Proof
body_md:
Using (\ref{Poisson1}) and moving the ``mass'' to the positive $y$ axis
 we may write 
\begin{equation}
\label{Poisson2}
\log| h'(\zeta)|\geq \frac {\sigma} \pi\int_{0}^\infty\frac{\Psi (s)}
{\sigma^2 + (s+t\sigma)^2}ds \qquad(\zeta\in S_\varepsilon),
\end{equation}
where $\Psi(s)=\log|h'(is)+\log|h'(-is)|$, $|\zeta|=|\sigma + it\sigma|$ and 
$\displaystyle{t=\tan(\frac\pi 2 - \varepsilon)}$.

Integrating (\ref{Poisson2}) by parts, the right side of (\ref{Poisson2}) becomes
\begin{equation}
\label{Poisson3}\
\frac \sigma\pi\left(\frac{\int_0^s\Psi(x)dx}{\sigma^2+(s+t\sigma)^2}\bigg |_0^\infty+2\int_0^\infty
\frac{(s+t\sigma)\int_0^s\Psi(x)dx}{(\sigma^2+(s+t\sigma)^2)^2}ds\right).
\end{equation}
From the elimination of Case 1, it follows that the first term in (\ref{Poisson3}) vanishes.

Regarding the second term, using the elimination of Case 2 we can write
$$
\frac{2\sigma}\pi\int_0^\infty
\frac{(s+t\sigma)\int_0^s\Psi(x)dx}{(\sigma^2+(s+\sigma t)^2)^2}ds \geq (1+o(1))\frac{2\sigma}\pi
\int_0^\infty\frac{(s+t\sigma)Cs}{(\sigma^2+(s+t\sigma)^2)^2}ds
$$
as $\sigma\to\infty$.

Since
$$
\sigma\int_0^\infty\frac{(s+t\sigma)s}{(\sigma^2+(s+t\sigma)^2)^2}ds=
\frac 1 2\left (\arctan(s/\sigma+t)-\frac{s\sigma}{\sigma^2+(s+t\sigma)^2}\right )\bigg |_{s=0}^\infty
=\pi/2-\arctan ( t)
$$
Lemma 6 follows.
\qed
